correctness.rationale: For a>b>0, the low-flow time coordinate h(F)=integral dF/min(b,f(F)) transforms the low-intensity flow to translation and the higher flow to a positive nonincreasing velocity ratio R. The high-flow map has derivative R(Psi_s(w))/R(w)<=1, proving the adjacent interchange and exact strictness integral; strictly monotone state propagators allow bubble sorting over all finite storms. A rational capacity witness yields precisely 1/16 infiltration advantage. The standalone checker confirms the fraction identities and 2,625 finite numerical comparisons with stated tolerance; the theorem is proved analytically, not inferred from tests. No ponding or soil recovery is assumed.

value.rationale: Storm temporal order controls total infiltration-excess volume even at identical total rain and durations. The theorem supplies rigorous best/worst designs and a sharp equality criterion for the physically motivated no-ponding infiltration-capacity model, with strict exact 1/16 witness. It supports model benchmarks and controlled rainfall comparisons while explicitly not predicting peak floods or full porous-media dynamics.
